turn: In 6,352 rated moments of recorded support conversations (ESConv), what the supporter did added nothing to the person's own next rating: −0.0008 [−0.0036, +0.0019] in prediction error, inside the ±0.01 band where it counts as no effect; letting the effect change over the conversation added nothing either (TURN_RATINGS).
cue: Closing the model's cue loophole (person model v3: a cue ends on its own after 6 ticks) removed stuck cues (15 of 15 runs → 0), but cut open-cue ticks only 1.8×, short of the 10× target. Always Bear still beats the Watchdog, by 0.019 per tick instead of 0.041: about half of its earlier lead was the loophole (CUE_RESOLVE).
run_note: These recorded runs use person model v2, where an uninterrupted cue blocks later cues. With that loophole closed (v3), stuck cues fall from 15 of 15 runs to 0 and always Bear's lead over the Watchdog halves (0.041 → 0.019 per tick; CUE_RESOLVE).
lab_note: In people's own ratings in ESConv, the supporter's action made no measurable difference to the next rating (TURN_RATINGS), which is what the equal effects assume. The different effects remain invented.
